```{r}
#library(renv)

library(tidyverse)

set.seed(123)
```

# Aim and data source

The aim of this script is to analyze bulk RNA-seq data from human embryonic fibroblasts with **Merkel cell polyomavirus** (MCPyV) **truncated large tumor antigen (TLT)**, **early region (ER)**, and **GFP control** inducible vectors. We will look for genes and pathways associated with proteostasis, particularly with interest in aggresome, unfolded protein response, and autophagy using annotated gene sets. The data was downloaded from the GEO database, series [GSE130639](http://ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE130639). The data is described in more detail in Yang et al., 2025 [(doi: 10.1172/JCI177724)](https://doi.org/10.1172/jci177724).

We will focus on samples at 24 and 48 hours after induction of TLT, ER, or the control vectors. 

# Summary of main findings

In the following analysis we show these main findings:

- UPR response, as defined by Hallmark gene sets, is upregulated in ER vs. GFP (@fig-ERHbar) and downregulated in TLT vs. GFP (@fig-TLTHbar), however the running enrichment score shows these enrichments to be bidirectional, with gene hits at both extremes (@fig-ERHUPR, @fig-TLTHUPR).

- Enriched proteostasis-related GO terms showed upregulation of chaperones and their binding, but a decrease in autophagy (@fig-ERGOprotbar, @fig-TLTGOprotbar). Similar patterns were observed for proteostasis-related Reactome terms (@fig-ERRprotbar, @fig-TLTRprotbar).

- Top-ranked genes in the select proteostasis-related pathways mostly shared expression patterns across ER and TLT replicates (@fig-TOPgeneHeatmap). The shown pathways were selected to be minimally overlapping (@fig-ERemap, @fig-TLTemap) to broadly cover most of the enriched terms in both comparisons.

- Aggresome-specific signature was positively associated to TLT or ER expression, but not significant (@fig-ERagg, @fig-TLTagg).

- Although not all samples at 48hrs post induction were available, the available samples show the same trends in proteostasis pathways as the 24hr-timepoint highlighted in the results above.


# Data loading

Raw counts were downloaded from GEO. Information on sample identity and gene IDs provided from the accession were also used.

```{r}
# load in counts
counts_full <- read.csv(
  here("Data", "GSE130639_raw_counts_GRCh38.p13_NCBI.csv"),
  sep = ";"
)
# load sample identifiers
sample_ids <- read.csv(here("Data", "GSE130639_series_matrix.csv"), sep = ";")[,
  1:2
]
# load gene names and symbols
gene_symbols <- read.csv(
  here("Data", "Human.GRCh38.p13.annot_mod.csv"),
  sep = ";"
)
```

Convert gene names to symbols and column names to more descriptive sample names. Summarize any duplicate gene symbol names. These duplicates are handled by summation of counts.
```{r}
library(dplyr)

#Two gene names are duplicated
gene_symbols[which(duplicated(gene_symbols$Symbol)), ]

new_names <- setNames(sample_ids$sample_id, sample_ids$sample_type)

counts <- counts_full %>%
  #convert gene names to symbols
  left_join(gene_symbols, by = "GeneID") %>%
  select(Symbol, everything(), -GeneID) %>%
  #change column names to more descriptive sample names
  dplyr::rename(any_of(new_names)) %>%
  #get rid of duplicates by summing them
  group_by(Symbol) %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), sum), .groups = "drop") %>%
  column_to_rownames("Symbol")

#write.csv(counts, here("Outputs", "GSE130639_rawcounts_formatted_20260911.csv"))
```
Next, the samples of interest will be extracted and analyzed.


# 24hr timepoint

Next I am only selecting the 24hr timepoint, as 48hr samples are incomplete. These are the available samples:
```{r}
count_24 <- counts %>%
  dplyr::select(matches("^(ER|TLT|GFP)_(24)_"))
#display included samples
count_24 %>% colnames
```

## DESeq2 for normalization and DEG

Next, DESeq2 is used for data normalization and differential gene expression analysis.

Conditions are defined.

```{r}
#| message: false
library("DESeq2")

metadata <- data.frame(condition = factor(gsub("_24_(1|2|3)", "", colnames(count_24))), 
                      replicate = factor(gsub("[A-Za]+_24_", "", colnames(count_24)))) 
rownames(metadata) <- colnames(count_24)

dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = as.matrix(count_24),
                              colData = metadata,
                              design = ~ condition)
```

Low-expressed genes are filtered and the model is fitted.
```{r}
#| message: false
# Remove genes have less than 3 samples with 10 counts or more
keep <- rowSums(counts(dds) >= 10) >= 3
dds <- dds[keep,]

#Deseq function automatically estimates size factors and dispersions
dds <- DESeq(dds)
```

Additionally, data is normalized and transformed for eventual heatmap plotting.
```{r}
#transform counts using vst
vsd <- vst(dds)
transformed_counts <- assay(vsd)
```

## DEGs

Look at top ten genes in the two main comparisons of interest (ER vs. GFP and TLT vs. GFP).

ER results:
```{r}
res_ER <- results(dds, alpha = 0.05, contrast = c("condition","ER", "GFP"))
summary(res_ER)

#top10 genes
res_ER[order(res_ER$pvalue),] %>% head(10)
```

Interactive table for **ER vs. GFP (padj < 0.05, abs(log2FoldChange) > 1)**:
```{r}
library(DT)

res_ER_dt <- res_ER %>% as.data.frame %>% filter(padj < 0.05, abs(log2FoldChange) > 1) %>% select(baseMean, log2FoldChange, pvalue, padj) %>% mutate(baseMean = round(baseMean, 3), log2FoldChange = round(log2FoldChange,3), pvalue = round(pvalue,5), padj = round(padj,5)) %>% tibble::rownames_to_column("gene")

datatable(
  res_ER_dt,
  filter = "top",
  options = list(
    pageLength = 10, 
    scrollX = TRUE
  ),
  rownames = TRUE
)
```

TLT results:
```{r}
res_TLT <- results(dds, alpha = 0.05, contrast = c("condition","TLT", "GFP"))
summary(res_TLT)

res_TLT[order(res_TLT$pvalue),] %>% head(10)
```

Interactive table for **TLT vs. GFP (padj < 0.05, abs(log2FoldChange) > 1)**:
```{r}
res_TLT_dt <- res_TLT %>% as.data.frame %>% filter(padj < 0.05, abs(log2FoldChange) > 1) %>% select(baseMean, log2FoldChange, pvalue, padj) %>% mutate(baseMean = round(baseMean, 3), log2FoldChange = round(log2FoldChange,3), pvalue = round(pvalue,5), padj = round(padj,5)) %>% tibble::rownames_to_column("gene")

datatable(
  res_TLT_dt,
  filter = "top",
  options = list(
    pageLength = 10, 
    scrollX = TRUE
  ),
  rownames = TRUE
)
```

In both comparisons, there are more downregulated genes (e.g. higher in control). 

## Over-representation analysis

First extract all significantly differentially expressed genes. (padj < 0.05, abs(log2FoldChange) > 1) Also extract the universes for both comparisons.
```{r}
#| message: false

library(clusterProfiler)
library(enrichplot)
library(msigdbr)

# convert results to tibble
deg_ER <- res_ER %>% 
  as_tibble(rownames = "gene")

#extract up and down-regulated genes
up_ER <- deg_ER %>%
  filter(padj < 0.05, log2FoldChange > 1) %>% 
  pull(gene)

down_ER <- deg_ER %>%
  filter(padj < 0.05, log2FoldChange < -1) %>% 
  pull(gene)

#extract all genes in the universe
universe_ER <- deg_ER %>% pull(gene)

#same for TLT cmparison
deg_TLT <- res_TLT %>% 
  as_tibble(rownames = "gene")

up_TLT <- deg_TLT %>%
  filter(padj < 0.05, log2FoldChange > 1) %>% 
  pull(gene)

down_TLT <- deg_TLT %>%
  filter(padj < 0.05, log2FoldChange < -1) %>% 
  pull(gene)

universe_TLT <- deg_TLT %>% pull(gene)
```

### Hallmark gene sets

First will look at Hallmark gene sets, particularly interested in unfolded protein response.

Hallmark gene sets in ER vs. GFP:

#### Up in ER
```{r}
msig_h <- msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", collection = "H")
ORA_H_up_ER <- enricher(
  gene = up_ER,            # can use SYMBOL here
  TERM2GENE = msig_h[, c("gs_name", "gene_symbol")],
  universe = universe_ER,
  pAdjustMethod = "BH",
  pvalueCutoff = 0.05
```

### Reactome gene sets

Particularly interested in terms that have to do with unfolded response, autophagy, chaperones, heat shock, proteosome, aggresome, etc.

Comparison for ER:

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Up in ER

```{r}
#| fig-height: 8
#| warning: false
msig_react <- msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", category = "C2", subcategory = "CP:REACTOME")

ORA_R_up_ER <- enricher(
  gene = up_ER,            # can use SYMBOL here
  TERM2GENE = msig_react[, c("gs_name", "gene_symbol")],
  universe = universe_ER,
  pAdjustMethod = "BH",
  pvalueCutoff = 0.05
)

enrichplot::dotplot(ORA_R_up_ER, showCategory = 20, title = "Upregulated genes in ER (top 20 reactome)")
```

Which of all enriched reactome terms are connected to the pathways of interest?
```{r}
# are any enriched terms involved in unfolded protein response
as.data.frame(ORA_R_up_ER) %>%
  filter(grepl("UNFOLD|AUTOPHAG|PROTEO|HEAT.?SHOCK|HSP|ER.?STRESS|UPR|CHAPER|AGGRE|MISFOLD", Description)) %>%
  select(Description, GeneRatio, pvalue, p.adjust)
```

Found one term that has to do with HSF1-mediated heat shock in genes upregulated in ER. DEGs involved in this pathway are the following:

```{r}
cnetplot(ORA_R_up_ER, showCategory = "REACTOME_REGULATION_OF_HSF1_MEDIATED_HEAT_SHOCK_RESPONSE")
```

## GSEA

Next will perform GSEA on similar genesets in the two condition comparisons. Genes will be ranked by DESeq2 test statistic to incorporate information from both Log2FC and significance.

### Hallmark GSEA

First derive ranked list from **ER vs. GFP** and check top and bottom genes.
```{r}
ranked_ER <- deg_ER %>% 
  # extract statistic
  pull(stat) %>% 
  # add names 
  setNames(deg_ER$gene) %>% 
  # sort in decreasing order
  sort(decreasing = T)

#show top and bottom genes to verify behavior
head(ranked_ER)
tail(ranked_ER)
```

Next evaluate Hallmark gene set enrichment.

```{r}
#| fig-height: 7.8
#| warning: false
gsea_H_ER <- GSEA(
  ranked_ER,
  TERM2GENE = msig_h[, c("gs_name", "gene_symbol")],
  verbose = FALSE,
  pvalueCutoff = 0.05,
  pAdjustMethod = "BH",
  method = "multilevel")

dotplot(gsea_H_ER, showCategory = 20, title = "Hallmark gene sets:\nER vs. GFP" , split=".sign") + facet_grid(.~.sign)
```

The unfolded protein response is higher in ER samples.

List the results, including the NES and adjusted p-value.
```{r}
as.data.frame(gsea_H_ER) %>%
  dplyr::select(enrichmentScore, NES, pvalue, p.adjust, log2err)
```

Barplot for cleaner visualization
```{r}
#| fig-height: 5.4
#| fig-width: 5.6
#| label: fig-ERHbar
#| fig-cap: Bar plot of NES scores of Hallmark gene sets in ER vs. GFP.
gsea_H_ER_res <- as.data.frame(gsea_H_ER)
bar_plot <- tibble(term = str_to_title(gsub("_"," ", gsub("HALLMARK", "", rownames(gsea_H_ER_res)))),
                  NES = gsea_H_ER_res$NES, 
                  padj = gsea_H_ER_res$p.adjust)

bar_plot$term <- factor(bar_plot$term, 
                  levels = bar_plot$term[order(bar_plot$NES, decreasing = F)])

p <- ggplot(bar_plot, aes(x = NES, y = term, fill = padj)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#0000E6", 
        high = "#C5C5C7", 
        mid = "#7575EB", 
        midpoint = 0.025) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, 
      color = "black", 
      linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "ER vs. GFP",
      subtitle = "Hallmark gene set enrichment",
      x = "Normalized Enrichment Score", 
      y = "", 
      fill = "Adjusted p-value:") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5), 
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5), 
        axis.text = element_text(size = 10), 
        legend.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

p

#ggsave(here("Figures","LTST_ER_GSEA_hallmark_full_barplot.pdf"), p, width = 5.6, height = 5.4, units = "in")
```

Export enrichment results as tsv.
```{r}

```

```{r}
        midpoint = 0.025) +

      color = "black", 
      linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "TLT vs. GFP",
      subtitle = "Hallmark gene set enrichment",
      x = "Normalized Enrichment Score", 
      y = "", 
      fill = "Adjusted p-value:") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5), 
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5), 
        axis.text = element_text(size = 10), 
        legend.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

p

```


Detailed enrichment plot of UPR.
```{r}

#| fig-height: 3.5
#| label: fig-TLTHUPR
#| fig-cap: GSEA plot of UPR Hallmark gene set in TLT vs. GFP.
p <- gseaplot2(gsea_H_TLT,
  geneSetID = "HALLMARK_UNFOLDED_PROTEIN_RESPONSE", 
  title = "TLT vs. GFP",
```

The pattern seems to go in both directions.

Which genes are in the leading edge?
```{r}
#| message: false
cnetplot(gsea_H_TLT, showCategory = "HALLMARK_UNFOLDED_PROTEIN_RESPONSE", foldChange = ranked_TLT) + 
  scale_color_gradient2(name = "stat",
  low = "blue",
  mid = "white",
  high = "red")
```

#### Conclusion

Hallmark unfolded protein response picks up genes from both upregulated and downregulated areas. In ER vs. GFP, it is overall more activated, but in TLT vs. GFP it is more suppressed. However the difference may be only due to a few genes, as the leading edge genes in both comparisons are distinct.

### Heatmap of top genes in GSEA GO hits

First we evaluate the similarity of the enriched relevant terms to guide the decision on which to plot.
```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-height: 12
#| fig-width: 12
#| label: fig-ERemap
#| fig-cap: Enrichment map of enriched proteostasis-related GO terms in ER vs. GFP. 
# create a subset of the enrichment results with the relevant terms
gsea_GO_ER_sub <- gsea_GO_ER
gsea_GO_ER_sub@result <- gsea_GO_ER_sub@result[gsea_GO_ER_sub@result$ID %in% rownames(gsea_GO_ER_res), ]

# calculate similarity between terms
gsea_sim <- pairwise_termsim(gsea_GO_ER_sub)
#plot
emapplot(gsea_sim, size_edge = 2)
```

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-height: 12
#| fig-width: 12
#| label: fig-TLTemap
#| fig-cap: Enrichment map of enriched proteostasis-related GO terms in TLT vs. GFP. 
# create a subset of the enrichment results with the relevant terms
gsea_GO_TLT_sub <- gsea_GO_TLT
gsea_GO_TLT_sub@result <- gsea_GO_TLT_sub@result[gsea_GO_TLT_sub@result$ID %in% rownames(gsea_GO_TLT_res), ]

# calculate similarity between terms
gsea_sim <- pairwise_termsim(gsea_GO_TLT_sub)
#plot
emapplot(gsea_sim, size_edge = 2)
```

Selected pathways based on emapplot and cnet plots to represent both sides of processes, minimize gene overlap and cover as much of the map possible for both comparisons. These are:

```{r}
selected_terms <- c("GOCC_AUTOPHAGOSOME", "GOBP_MACROAUTOPHAGY" , "GOBP_REGULATION_OF_AUTOPHAGY", "GOMF_HEAT_SHOCK_PROTEIN_BINDING", "GOMF_ATP_DEPENDENT_PROTEIN_FOLDING_CHAPERONE", "GOBP_CELLULAR_RESPONSE_TO_UNFOLDED_PROTEIN")
selected_terms
```

Extract top 10 genes from the leading edge of each of these terms in both comparisons. Remove repeating genes.
```{r}
# extract the leading edge genes - these are ordered by rank
core_enrichment_ER <- gsea_GO_ER_sub@result[gsea_GO_ER_sub@result$ID %in% selected_terms, c("core_enrichment", "ID")]
core_enrichment_TLT <- gsea_GO_TLT_sub@result[gsea_GO_TLT_sub@result$ID %in% selected_terms, c("core_enrichment", "ID")]

#split into individual genes and extract top 10
top10_genes_ER <- lapply(
    core_enrichment_ER$core_enrichment,
    function(x) strsplit(x, "/")[[1]][1:10]
)
# name list by ID
names(top10_genes_ER) <- core_enrichment_ER$ID

top10_genes_ER

top10_genes_TLT <- lapply(
    core_enrichment_TLT$core_enrichment,
    function(x) strsplit(x, "/")[[1]][1:10]
)

names(top10_genes_TLT) <- core_enrichment_TLT$ID

top10_genes_TLT
```

### GSEA with single term

We found a reference for an extended list of genes (36) in the **GOCC Aggresome term**. We will manually run it as a single set. According to the [database](https://maayanlab.cloud/Harmonizome/gene_set/aggresome/GO+Cellular+Component+Annotations+2023), this is a GOCC Annotation from 2023. It provides and external link to the [source](http://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO:0016235), which however contains fewer genes.

Make the gene set:
```{r}
genes <- c("BAG3","CABIN1","CARD14","DVL2","EDEM1","EEF2","EPS15","FGR","HDAC6","HOXC9","HOXD3","HSPA1A","HSPA1B","HSPB7","KLF8","KLHL14","PARK2","POLD1","PRDM16","PRKCQ","PSEN1","RANGAP1","RNF32","SFMBT2","SLC2A14","SLC2A3","SQSTM1","STRADB","TDP2","TRIM37","TRIM66","UBD","UBQLN1","URB2","XRN2","ZBTB14")

sig_aggresome <- tibble(gs_name = "GOCC_AGGRESOME", gene = genes)
```

First **ER vs. GFP** comparison.

Run GSEA and investigate detailed plot.
```{r}
#| fig-height: 9
#| warning: false
library(fgsea)

fgsea(pathways = list(Aggresome = sig_aggresome$gene),
stats = ranked_ER)

gsea_aggresome <- GSEA(
ranked_ER,
TERM2GENE = sig_aggresome,
verbose = FALSE,
pvalueCutoff = 1,
pAdjustMethod = "BH"
)
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| label: fig-ERagg
#| fig-cap: GSEA plot of GOCC Aggresome gene set in ER vs. GFP.
p <- gseaplot2(gsea_aggresome,
  geneSetID = 1, 
  title = "ER vs. GFP", 
  pvalue_table = T,
  rel_heights = c(1.2, 0.2, 0.5))
p

#ggsave(here("Figures","LTST_ER_GSEA_singleTerm_Aggresome.pdf"), p, width = 3.7, height = 2.7, units = "in")
```

```{r}
#| warning: false
cnetplot(gsea_aggresome, foldChange = ranked_ER) + 
  scale_color_gradient2(name = "stat",
  low = "blue",
  mid = "white",
  high = "red")
```

Now for **TLT vs. GFP**.

Run GSEA and investigate detailed plot.
```{r}
#| fig-height: 9
#| warning: false
library(fgsea)

fgsea(pathways = list(Aggresome = sig_aggresome$gene),
stats = ranked_TLT)

gsea_aggresome <- GSEA(
ranked_TLT,
TERM2GENE = sig_aggresome,
verbose = FALSE,
pvalueCutoff = 1,
pAdjustMethod = "BH"
)
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| label: fig-TLTagg
#| fig-cap: GSEA plot of GOCC Aggresome gene set in TLT vs. GFP.

  geneSetID = 1, 
  title = "TLT vs. GFP", 
  pvalue_table = T,
  rel_heights = c(1.2, 0.2, 0.5))
p
```


#### Conclusion

The enrichment is not statistically significant, but there do seem to be more terms in the upregulated genes.

# 48hr timepoint

Next I am only selecting the 48hr timepoint, despite it being incomplete. I will only use this analysis for GSEA, which does not have the same statistical requirements.

```{r}
count_48 <- counts %>%
  dplyr::select(matches("^(ER|TLT|GFP)_(48)_"))
count_48 %>% colnames
```


## DEseq for normalization and DEG

```{r}
#| message: false
metadata <- data.frame(condition = factor(gsub("_48_(1|2|3)", "", colnames(count_48))), 
                      replicate = factor(gsub("[A-Za]+_48_", "", colnames(count_48)))) 
rownames(metadata) <- colnames(count_48)

dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = as.matrix(count_48),
                              colData = metadata,
                              design = ~ condition)
```
```{r}
# Remove genes have less than 2 samples with 10 counts or more
keep <- rowSums(counts(dds) >= 10) >= 2
dds <- dds[keep,]

#Deseq function automatically estimates size factors and dispersios
dds <- DESeq(dds)
```

## DEGs for ranked list

Look at top ten genes in the two main comparisons of interest.
```{r}
res_ER_48 <- results(dds, alpha = 0.05, contrast = c("condition","ER", "GFP"))
summary(res_ER_48)

#top10 genes
res_ER_48[order(res_ER_48$pvalue),] %>% head(10)
```

TLT results:
```{r}
res_TLT_48 <- results(dds, alpha = 0.05, contrast = c("condition","TLT", "GFP"))
summary(res_TLT_48)

res_TLT_48[order(res_TLT_48$pvalue),] %>% head(10)
```

## GSEA

Next will perform GSEA on similar genesets in the two condition comparisons. Genes will be ranked by test statistic to incorporate information from both Log2FC and significance, despite not having full sample sets.

### Hallmark GSEA

First derive ranked list from **ER vs. GFP** and check top and bottom genes.
```{r}
deg_ER_48 <- res_ER_48 %>% 
  as_tibble(rownames = "gene")

ranked_ER_48 <- deg_ER_48 %>% 
  # extract statistic
  pull(stat) %>% 
  # add names 
  setNames(deg_ER_48$gene) %>% 
  # sort in decreasing order
  sort(decreasing = T)

#show top and bottom genes to verify behavior
head(ranked_ER_48)
tail(ranked_ER_48)
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 10
#| warning: false
gsea_H_ER_48 <- GSEA(
  ranked_ER_48,
  TERM2GENE = msig_h[, c("gs_name", "gene_symbol")],
  verbose = FALSE,
  pvalueCutoff = 0.05,
  pAdjustMethod = "BH",
  method = "multilevel")

dotplot(gsea_H_ER_48, showCategory = 20, title = "Hallmark gene sets:\nER vs. GFP (48hr)" , split=".sign") + facet_grid(.~.sign)
```

The unfolded protein response is higher in ER samples as in the 24hr timepoint.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
gseaplot2(gsea_H_ER_48,
  geneSetID = "HALLMARK_UNFOLDED_PROTEIN_RESPONSE", 
  title = "ER vs. GFP (48hr)", 
  pvalue_table = T,
  rel_heights = c(2, 0.5, 0.5))
```

Which genes are in the leading edge?
```{r}
#| message: false
cnetplot(gsea_H_ER_48, showCategory = "HALLMARK_UNFOLDED_PROTEIN_RESPONSE", foldChange = ranked_ER_48) + 
  scale_color_gradient2(name = "stat",
  low = "blue",
  mid = "white",
  high = "red")
```

Now for **TLT vs. GFP** comparison at 48hrs. First prepare ranked gene list and check top and bottom genes.
```{r}
deg_TLT_48 <- res_TLT_48 %>% 
  as_tibble(rownames = "gene")

ranked_TLT_48 <- deg_TLT_48 %>% 
  # extract statistic
  pull(stat) %>% 
  # add names 
  setNames(deg_TLT_48$gene) %>% 
  # sort in decreasing order
  sort(decreasing = T)

#show top and bottom genes to verify behavior
head(ranked_TLT_48)
tail(ranked_TLT_48)
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 8.5
#| warning: false
gsea_H_TLT_48 <- GSEA(
  ranked_TLT_48,
  TERM2GENE = msig_h[, c("gs_name", "gene_symbol")],
  verbose = FALSE,
  pvalueCutoff = 0.05,
  pAdjustMethod = "BH",
  method = "multilevel")

dotplot(gsea_H_TLT_48, showCategory = 20, title = "Hallmark gene sets:\nTLT vs. GFP (48hr)" , split=".sign") + facet_grid(.~.sign)
```

The there is no difference in UPR in contrast to the ER vs. GFP comparison or the TLT vs. GFP comparison at 24hrs.

#### Conclusion

Hallmark unfolded response picks up genes from both upregulated and downregulated areas, but is significantly positively enriched in the ER vs. GFP comparison (same as 24hrs). It is not significant for TLT vs. GFP, which previously (24hrs) showed downregulation.

### Reactome gene sets

First for **ER vs. GFP**.

```{r}
#| fig-height: 12
#| warning: false
gsea_R_ER_48 <- GSEA(
  ranked_ER_48,
  TERM2GENE = msig_react[, c("gs_name", "gene_symbol")],
  verbose = FALSE,
  pvalueCutoff = 0.05,
  pAdjustMethod = "BH",
  method = "multilevel")

dotplot(gsea_R_ER_48, showCategory = 15, title = "Reactome gene sets:\nER vs. GFP (48hr)" , split=".sign") + facet_grid(.~.sign)
```

There don't seem to be relevant terms in the top 15.

Relevant terms:
```{r}
gsea_R_ER_res_48 <- as.data.frame(gsea_R_ER_48) %>%
  filter(grepl("UNFOLD|AUTOPHAG|PROTEOS|HEAT.?SHOCK|HSP|ER.?STRESS|UPR|CHAPER|AGGRES|MISFOLD", Description)) %>%
  select( enrichmentScore, NES, pvalue, p.adjust, log2err)

gsea_R_ER_res_48
```

The HSF-1 mediated heat shock term comes up again as upregulated, autophagy terms are downregulated. This is consistent with results at 24hrs. The difference here is that UPR is downregulated, unlike the Hallmarks at 24 and 48 hrs suggested.

Detailed GSEA plot.
```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
gseaplot2(gsea_R_ER_48,
  geneSetID = rownames(gsea_R_ER_res_48), 
  title = "ER vs. GFP (48 hrs)", 
  pvalue_table = T,
  rel_heights = c(2, 0.5, 0.5))
```

Which genes are in the leading edges?
```{r}
cnetplot(gsea_R_ER_48, showCategory = rownames(gsea_R_ER_res_48), foldChange = ranked_ER_48) + 
  scale_color_gradient2(name = "stat",
  low = "blue",
  mid = "white",
  high = "red")
```

Now Reactome for **TLT vs. GFP** comparison.

```{r}
#| fig-height: 12
#| warning: false
gsea_R_TLT_48 <- GSEA(
  ranked_TLT_48,
  TERM2GENE = msig_react[, c("gs_name", "gene_symbol")],
  verbose = FALSE,
  pvalueCutoff = 0.05,
  pAdjustMethod = "BH",
  method = "multilevel")

dotplot(gsea_R_TLT_48, showCategory = 15, title = "Reactome gene sets:\nTLT vs. GFP (48hr)" , split=".sign") + facet_grid(.~.sign)
```

There are no ubviously relevant terms in the top genes.

Relevant terms:
```{r}
gsea_R_TLT_res_48 <- as.data.frame(gsea_R_TLT_48) %>%
  filter(grepl("UNFOLD|AUTOPHAG|PROTEOS|HEAT.?SHOCK|HSP|ER.?STRESS|UPR|CHAPER|AGGRES|MISFOLD", Description)) %>%
  select( enrichmentScore, NES, pvalue, p.adjust, log2err)

gsea_R_TLT_res_48
```

A heat shock pathway is upregulated, while an autophagy term is downregulated. This is consistent with the 24 hr timepoint. Additionally, UPR snd some chaperones are downregulated, which is different to 24hrs.

Detaled GSEA plot:
```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
gseaplot2(gsea_R_TLT_48,
  geneSetID = rownames(gsea_R_TLT_res_48), 
  title = "TLT vs. GFP (48hr)", 
  pvalue_table = T,
  rel_heights = c(2, 0.5, 0.5))
```

Which genes are in the leading edges?
```{r}
cnetplot(gsea_R_TLT_48, showCategory = rownames(gsea_R_TLT_res_48), foldChange = ranked_TLT_48) + 
  scale_color_gradient2(name = "stat",
  low = "blue",
  mid = "white",
  high = "red")
```

#### Conclusion

In both TLT and ER comparisons, the one heat shock pathways is consistently upregulated, while autophagy terms are downregulated. This is consistent with 24 hrs. The consistency with chaperone pathways and UPR are less clear.

```{r}
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, 
      color = "black", 
      linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "TLT vs. GFP (48hr)",
      subtitle = "GO: relevant enriched terms",
      x = "Normalized Enrichment Score", 
      y = "", 
      fill = "Adjusted p-value:") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5), 
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5), 
        axis.text = element_text(size = 10), 
        legend.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

p

#ggsave(here("Figures","LTST_TLT_48hr_GSEA_GO_select_barplot.pdf"), p, width = 7.8, height = 4.5, units = "in")
```

For next plots, splitting by p-value to show individual enrichments in detailed GSEA plots.
```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
gseaplot2(gsea_GO_TLT_48,
  geneSetID = rownames(gsea_GO_TLT_res_48)[1:8], 
  title = "TLT vs. GFP (48hr)", 
  pvalue_table = T,
  rel_heights = c(2, 0.5, 0.5))

  gseaplot2(gsea_GO_TLT_48,
  geneSetID = rownames(gsea_GO_TLT_res_48)[9:16], 
  title = "TLT vs. GFP (48hr)", 
  pvalue_table = T,
  rel_heights = c(2, 0.5, 0.5))

  gseaplot2(gsea_GO_TLT_48,
  geneSetID = rownames(gsea_GO_TLT_res_48)[17:23], 
  title = "TLT vs. GFP (48hr)", 
  pvalue_table = T,
  rel_heights = c(2, 0.5, 0.5))
```

Which genes are in the leading edges? 
```{r}
#| message: false
cnetplot(gsea_GO_TLT_48, showCategory = rownames(gsea_GO_TLT_res_48) , foldChange = ranked_TLT_48) + 
  scale_color_gradient2(name = "stat",
  low = "blue",
  mid = "white",
  high = "red")

cnetplot(gsea_GO_TLT_48, showCategory = rownames(gsea_GO_TLT_res_48[gsea_GO_TLT_res_48$NES > 0,]) , foldChange = ranked_TLT_48) + 
  scale_color_gradient2(name = "stat",
  low = "blue",
  mid = "white",
  high = "red")

#strange behaviour with all 15 negative terms plotting, so showing all but regulation of autophagy
cnetplot(gsea_GO_TLT_48, showCategory = rownames(gsea_GO_TLT_res_48[gsea_GO_TLT_res_48$NES < 0,])[c(1:8,10:5)] , foldChange = ranked_TLT_48) + 
  scale_color_gradient2(name = "stat",
  low = "blue",
  mid = "white",
  high = "red")
```

#### Conclusion

Autophagy patterns are consistent with 24 hr timepoint (downregulated). Chaperone pathways as well, but to a lesser degree.

### GSEA with single term

Same as for 24hr timepoint
Run GSEA and investigate detailed plot.
```{r}
#| fig-height: 9
#| warning: false

fgsea(pathways = list(Aggresome = sig_aggresome$gene),
stats = ranked_TLT_48)

gsea_aggresome <- GSEA(
ranked_TLT_48,
TERM2GENE = sig_aggresome,
verbose = FALSE,
pvalueCutoff = 1,
pAdjustMethod = "BH"
)

gseaplot2(gsea_aggresome, geneSetID = 1,  title = "TLT vs. GFP (Only one GS tested, 48hr)", 
  pvalue_table = T) 

cnetplot(gsea_aggresome, foldChange = ranked_TLT_48) + 
  scale_color_gradient2(name = "stat",
  low = "blue",
  mid = "white",
  high = "red")
```

#### Conclusion

The enrichment is not statistically significant, but there do seem to be more terms in the upregulated genes, as was the case for 24 hrs.
